steps.title: Running commands at the same time

content.value:
ParallelCommandGroup runs all its commands simultaneously.

It finishes only when every command inside it is done.

Unlike SequentialCommandGroup, all commands start on the same tick.

Declare two private DcMotor fields: frontLeft and frontRight.

In initialize(), get "front_left_motor" and "front_right_motor" from hardwareMap.

steps.title: Build two sequences and run them together

content.value:
Create two SequentialCommandGroups.

The first for frontLeft: InstantCommand (set power 0.5), WaitCommand(2000), InstantCommand (set power 0.0).

The second for frontRight: InstantCommand (set power 0.3), WaitCommand(1000), InstantCommand (set power 0.0).

Wrap both in a ParallelCommandGroup and schedule it.

Both motors start together. The shorter sequence finishes first, the longer one keeps going. The group finishes when both are done — after 2 seconds.

You can nest groups. A SequentialCommandGroup with a ParallelCommandGroup inside runs the parallel block, then continues.

For example: drive forward for 2 seconds, then turn AND spin together for 1 second, then stop. Each group is a building block that composes cleanly.
